title: SRE pulse — incident annotations, SLO posture, and handoff notes (week of 2029-08-21)
content:
Purpose: quick operational roundup for the SRE rotation covering the EdgeCache 503 event, current SLO posture, short-term mitigations, and handoff items for next-week on-call. Intended as a compact log (notes-to-self + action list) rather than a formal postmortem.

TL;DR
- Aug 20 11:10–11:40 UTC: transient 503 spike from EdgeCache cluster eu-west-1 (peak 4.3% error rate, primarily short lived). Root cause: concurrent eviction storm triggered by new LRU tweak in cache shard manager (deployed via infra canary).
- Impact: 12 customer routes saw degraded success ratios; p95 + p99 write latencies rose ~120ms and 260ms respectively. No data loss, most traffic served from fallback origin after circuit-breakers trip.
- SLO: hosted-api availability window consumed ~0.08% of daily error budget (~small but visible).
- Current action: rollback LRU tweak on canary hosts, throttled rollout paused, follow-up mitigation PR open (PR 2897).

Chronological notes (observational, raw)
- 2029-08-20 10:58 UTC — Ops alert: first 503 spike alerted by synthetic monitors (eu-west-1). Alert channel: #sre-ops.
- 2029-08-20 11:03 UTC — Oncall (Aisha) triaged, opened incident JIRA-INC-4312. Started bridge.
- 2029-08-20 11:07 UTC — Telemetry: memory churn + eviction counters jumped on cache-shard-12; correlates with infra canary rollout 11:00 UTC.
- 2029-08-20 11:10 UTC — Circuit breakers triggered for heavy routes; traffic shifted to origin; some customer clients experienced 503s while switching.
- 2029-08-20 11:20 UTC — Decided to rollback canary LRU change (rollback completed at 11:24 UTC).
- 2029-08-20 11:30–11:40 UTC — Error rate returned to baseline; bridge closed at 11:47 UTC after monitoring window.

Immediate root-cause hypothesis (short form)
- The LRU tweak changed eviction aggressiveness under bursty patterns; on a small subset of shards this produced an eviction cascade where objects were churned faster than upstream re-population, causing transient cache misses and higher upstream load. Unanticipated race in shard manager’s refill path amplified tail latencies.

Actions taken/completed
- Rolled back canary rollout within 25 minutes of detection.
- Throttled future canaries for cache-shard-manager to 1 host/hour until we validate fix.
- Opened infra PR 2897: bubble fix + additional observability (per-shard eviction histograms, refill latency metric).
- Notified affected customers via CS (ticket template used).

Open follow-ups (owner / ETA)
- Matt Hsu: add per-shard eviction histograms to Prometheus + grafana panels; ETA 2029-08-26.
- Brian Chen: patch to refill path race (PR 2897); ETA 2029-08-24 for unit tests, 2029-08-27 for staged deploy.
- Aisha Patel: update EdgeCache runbook with explicit canary throttles and rollback checklist; ETA 2029-08-23.
- Lena Ortiz: run a chaos test (eviction-heavy load) in staging to validate fix and surface any other race conditions; ETA 2029-08-29.

SLO posture (week snapshot)
- Hosted API availability SLO (99.95% monthly): This incident consumed ~0.08% of a day’s budget. Monthly rolling burn remains healthy but worth keeping eyes on as we approach end of month.
- Latency SLO (p99 < 500ms): Brief p99 increases during incident; no sustained violation.
- Error budget outlook: rolling 7-day burn is 0.12% — low but trending up from baseline (0.03% two weeks ago).

Operational recommendations
- Enforce canary throttling for any infra change touching cache or routing layers (new guardrail in CI).
- Add an automated canary-to-rollback pipeline: if per-shard eviction rate spikes >X within Y minutes, auto-pause rollout and alert with runbook link.
- Quick-win: add edge-level sticky routing fallback that prefers degarded-slow cached reads to avoid 503s during refill storms. Low-risk feature, Matt to prototype.

Handoff for next rotation (what to watch for)
- Monitor grafana panel: EdgeCache — per-shard eviction rate and refill-latency (dashboard link in runbook).
- Synthetic checks: observe eu-west-1 and us-west-2 synthetic read success ratio.
- Watch PR 2897 CI runs and staged deploy status; expect a small performance drift during unit tests.
- If any 503 > 1% sustained for 5 minutes, escalate to Bridge and follow runbook section 3 (manual rollback + traffic re-route).

Meeting notes (SRE sync 2029-08-21)
- Quick sync takeaway: align infra and serving runtime on churn-resistant cache defaults. Agreed: default LRU aggressiveness will be reduced and moved to a feature flag.
- Deploy windows: new policy — cache-impacting changes only between 03:00–09:00 UTC to minimize customer overlap.
- CS coordination: create a canned customer-facing summary for small-impact incidents (template ready).

Loose questions / items for Product/Platform discussion
- Is the current SLO margin for hosted-api adequate given expected Q4 traffic growth? Recommend product review with forecasting (product + finance).
- Should we invest in a lightweight local-memory tier for each shard to reduce refill pressure? Preliminary spike budget analysis needed.

Quick TODOs (near term)
- [Aisha] Update runbook + link dashboards (due 8/23).
- [Brian] Finalize PR 2897 and assign reviewers (due 8/24).
- [Matt] Prototype sticky-read fallback and triangle test in staging (due 8/30).
- [Lena] Schedule chaos test and post-results review (due 8/29).

Notes-to-self (unpolished)
- Keep rolling notes in this doc until retrospective drafted.
- Remember to include thermal/host-level metrics in next triage to rule out hardware-induced GC spikes.

End of weekly pulse. Ping me in #sre-ops or DM if you want a quick walkthrough of the bridge logs or sample traces.
